newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products close higher as soybeans gain.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products close higher as soybeans gain.

text.p: CBOT soy product futures closed higher on a correction from Wednesday's slide with gains in soybeans leading the way up, traders said.
Weather outlooks for cooler weather to move into the Midwest by the weekend also garnered attention as a bullish market factor, they said.

Also midday weather updates indicating diminishing possibilities for rain soon in eastern U.S. soy growing areas supported futures, they said. Some soy plants are in the pod filling stage and need rain to aid the process, sources said.
Rumors that China was seeking U.S. or South American soymeal for October shipment helped buoy soymeal futures.
Soyoil futures volume was estimated at 20,000 contracts, down from 23,566 Wednesday, the CBOT said. Soyoil options volume was estimated at 1,000, up from 705 Wednesday.
Soymeal futures volume was estimated at 23,000 contracts, down from 23,928 Wednesday, CBOT said. Soymeal options volume was estimated at 2,500 contracts, down from 2,633 Wednesday.
Soymeal futures closed $1.70 to $6.10 per ton higher, with September up $3.50 at $266.10 a ton.
Soyoil was 0.22 to 0.36 cent per lb higher, with September up 0.32 at 25.37 cents per lb.
